title: Google Gives IIT Kharagpur $5 Million to Accelerate AI Research and Training
excerpt: The funding, announced during the institute's 75th anniversary, covers AI research in Indic languages, agriculture and materials science, plus training and campus capacity building.
body:
• Google will provide IIT Kharagpur with $5 million (about Rs 46 crore) to develop and accelerate advanced AI research, the company announced on November 21.
  • The funding rests on three pillars: advanced AI research, educational opportunities, and AI capacity building across the campus.
  • Research will target Indic languages, materials science, agriculture and educational technology.
  • For IIT Kharagpur students and faculty, the money expands AI training and curriculum development; Google has not yet announced allocations for specific projects.

Google is providing the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur with $5 million in funding to help develop and accelerate advanced AI research, the company said in a blog post on November 21, during the institute's 75th anniversary celebrations.

"Google is providing the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (IIT Kharagpur) with USD 5 million in funding to help develop and accelerate advanced AI research, while cultivating India's next generation of scientific and technical talent," the company said, in a statement reported by The Hindu BusinessLine. The amount is about Rs 46 crore.

What the money is for

Google said the funding will support the institute's researchers and students across three core pillars. Under advanced AI research, it will back work on real-world challenges in Indic languages, materials science, agriculture and educational technology. Under educational opportunities, it will expand AI training and curriculum development for students, faculty and teachers. Under AI capacity building, it will support the university's AI frameworks and tooling across the campus.

"IIT Kharagpur is driving groundbreaking work in areas like Indic languages, agriculture, and education, and Google is excited to help accelerate this impact with a new partnership. Looking forward to seeing this collaboration shape the path for the next generation of students, just as IIT Kharagpur shaped my own."

— Sundar Pichai, CEO, Google and Alphabet

Speaking on the 75th anniversary of IIT Kharagpur, Director Suman Chakraborty said the fund support for applied AI research had been envisaged by the institute's alumnus and Google CEO Sundar Pichai, The Hindu BusinessLine reported.

Building on an existing partnership

The commitment builds on Google's existing research collaboration with IIT Kharagpur under its Amplify Initiative, which focuses on developing hyperlocal datasets representing India's linguistic and cultural diversity, according to Inc42. Inc42 also reported that no concrete plans for how exactly the cash will be used have been decided yet — so which labs and projects receive funding, and on what timeline, remains to be announced by the institute and Google.

The announcement lands as Google expands its wider AI commitments in India: the company has committed around $15 billion over five years, from 2026 to 2030, to establish an AI hub in Visakhapatnam, according to Madhyamam. For IIT Kharagpur, the immediate effect is a funded mandate across the three pillars; the test will be the project-level details the two sides publish next.
